extraction.Buyer: Phillip Points; $400.00 and ten head of ponies, in settlement of an old debt. Per source: 'Phillip Points, purchaser, turned out 10 ponies at my place in 1918. I have never seen them.' Effectively $400 cash plus undelivered ponies.
extraction.Occupation/Income: Supported by son. Husband contributes according to his ability but is in poor health. No support from government, state, or county.
extraction.Literate/Illiterate: Signed her own name (handwritten signature visible on source)
extraction.NOTES: Mental condition good; physical condition poor; in poor condition financially. Three sons dependent: ages 18, 16, 13. Doesn't think she was defrauded but does not think she received enough for the land — '$400.00 and ten head of ponies' was 'all I could get for it at the time.' Phillip Points (purchaser) turned out 10 ponies at her place in 1918, but she 'never seen them' — effectively the realized value was $400 cash. Document subscribed and sworn 26 November 1928 in Dawes County, Nebraska, before notary public (handwritten signature partially legible — appears to read 'Alvin S Fisher' or similar); commission expires 1/2/30. | IDENTITY RECOVERY 2026-04-27: Sonnet text-extraction captured the printed body of this questionnaire but failed to recover handwritten identifying information.
